abbreviations.IMFA: Institution-linked multi-affiliated output: publications in which at least one author affiliated with the university lists at least one additional affiliation on the same publication.
abbreviations.EC-CIS: Ecuador cross-institution signer output: publications signed with the university by an author who, in the same year, has another publication in the Ecuador-wide corpus on which their own affiliations exclude that university. Labelled "CIS" or "CIS-EC" in some files.
abbreviations.HPA: Hyperprolific-author-dependent output: publications that include at least one author with 25 or more publications attributed to the university in that year.
abbreviations.HAO: Hyper-authored output: publications with 100 or more distinct Scopus Author IDs.
abbreviations.NLO: Non-led output: publications with a classifiable corresponding-author affiliation and no corresponding author affiliated with the university. Labelled "non-lead" in some files.
abbreviations.CA known: Publications with at least one mappable corresponding-author affiliation; the denominator of NLO. Labelled "classifiable corresponding author" in some files.
abbreviations.HPA-MFA/EC-CIS: Publications signed by hyperprolific authors who are also multi-affiliated (MFA) or cross-institution signers. Labelled "HPA-MFA/CIS" or "HPA_MFA_or_CIS_articles" in some files.
abbreviations.IMFA or EC-CIS: Publications that are IMFA, EC-CIS or both.
abbreviations.CTA-1, CTA-5, CTA-10: Share of a university's publications signed by at least one of its 1, 5 or 10 most productive authors, counting each publication once. Labelled "CTA 1", "CTA 5" and "CTA 10" in the files.
abbreviations.A Top-50%: Smallest number of top-ranked authors whose publications jointly cover at least 50% of the university's output. Labelled "A top 50%" or "A_top50" in the files.
abbreviations.Top-1, Top-5: Share of the relevant publications linked to the leading partner affiliation or to the five leading partner affiliations. Labelled "top partner" and "top-5 partners" in the files.

codes.label: Institution codes
codes.text: Universities are identified by the codes U-01 to U-30, which are the same in the article and in all supplementary files.

aggregate.label: 30-university aggregate
aggregate.text: The 30-university aggregate, labelled "National" in the files, is the deduplicated union of the publications attributed to at least one of the 30 universities. It is not a national total.

partner_codes.label: Partner codes
partner_codes.text: Codes beginning with N- denote Ecuadorian affiliation entities outside the 30 universities.

blank.label: Blank cells
blank.text: A blank cell means that the value is undefined or that the institution-year was not eligible.

d.label: Robust deviation (D)
d.text: D = (x − median) / (IQR / 1.349), where x is the value of a university and the median and the interquartile range (IQR) are taken across the eligible universities in the same year or interval, excluding the 30-university aggregate. Eligibility requires at least 50 publications in the relevant denominator. A valid reference requires at least eight universities, two distinct values and a positive IQR. Elevated upper signal: D ≥ 2. Strong upper signal: D ≥ 3, labelled "extreme" in Tables S2, S3 and S7. Lower deviation: D ≤ −2. For HPA, HAO and HPA-MFA/EC-CIS, references use positive values only and lower deviations are not classified. D is descriptive; it is not a probability or a diagnostic test.

phases.label: Study phases
phases.text: The expansion phase runs from 2011 to 2018 and the slower-growth phase from 2018 to 2025. Annual transitions are grouped by their end year: 2012–2018 and 2019–2025. "Stabilization" in the files denotes the slower-growth phase.

interpretation.label: Interpretation
interpretation.text: The indicators describe bibliographic patterns of affiliation, authorship and concentration. A signal marks a deviation from the reference distribution of universities; it does not establish false affiliation, invalid authorship or misconduct.

source.label: Data source
source.text: Results calculated from Scopus records (Elsevier), retrieved through the Scopus API via http://api.elsevier.com and http://www.scopus.com. The retrieval dates are given in the Data availability statement of the article.
